slides.title:
Route customer requests
and learn from mistakes
slides.notes: The support team is fictional. The messages are public Banking77 data. We will make a genuine measured classifier comparison, then let participants run an open-ended data review experiment. Do not promise that every personal review will improve the score.

slides.title: The support queue needs a destination
slides.notes: Ask people what team should handle each request. These short examples explain the target before the model appears. We classify intent; we are not resolving accounts or giving financial advice. Source: PolyAI-LDN/task-specific-datasets.

slides.title: A manager has offered to automate forwarding
slides.notes: This is fictional dialogue. The engineering problem is a constrained label choice. A wrong label wastes time even if the message is polite and the JSON validates. Keep the humor in the manager line, and the task literal.

slides.title: The dataset contains 77 banking intents
slides.notes: The data are public queries, not attendee customer records. There are 77 classes. The official test set contains 40 examples per class. One low-resource training class has only 35 examples, which is why we reserve ten validation and ten review cases per class rather than twenty each.

slides.title: Give each partition one job
slides.notes: The split order was fixed before any model score. Ten examples of every intent go to validation and ten to the review pool. The test partition is only opened after selection freezes. Files are public for teaching; the code keeps final cases out of model-editing and labeling prompts.

slides.title: Open your copy and add your first trace
slides.notes: Let everyone open their own project. Hosted authentication is inherited; there is no shared gateway or host token. The $8 adjustable allowance covers fixed-model inference; CPU notebook charges are separate.

slides.title: The span should explain the operation
slides.notes: The notebook captures an independent event receipt and uses this participant-written function to export it. We compare stored spans with the receipt. A publication failure does not mean the operation failed or should be repeated.

slides.title: Read a request before revealing its label
slides.notes: Allow five minutes for individual predictions and partner discussion. The download includes 20 MB of cached features, original CSVs, license, and checksum manifest. Data loading sends no model call.

slides.title: Start with a word-based classifier
slides.notes: Explain unigrams and bigrams with card and my card. Fit the vectorizer only on training messages so validation vocabulary does not alter the feature space. This is a standard, inexpensive baseline, not a deliberately broken model.

slides.title: Then change the representation
slides.notes: Contrast sentence representation with lexical overlap. The cached encoder features are versioned and can be regenerated by the supplied preparation code. Cache lookup timing is not end-to-end encoder latency. The comparison changes representation, not data quantity or test cases.

slides.title: Implement the classifier head
slides.notes: The participant function is used in both actual fits. CPU training is bounded by iterations and two numerical-library threads. In preparation each fit took under four seconds with cached features; participant machines and hosting differ.

slides.title: Macro-F1 gives each intent equal weight
slides.notes: Do not average row-wise F1 values. Macro-F1 is computed from the whole matched prediction set. Accuracy is also reported. Neither metric tells the whole operational story because review can defer some cases.

slides.title: The worked comparison reduced routing mistakes
slides.notes: The fixed contract preceded final evaluation. Publish all six outcomes. Participants will inspect their own validation results first; the recorded result is a worked comparison and cannot be attributed to unexecuted learner edits. The deterministic seed repetitions check reproduction rather than uncertainty.

slides.title: A router can also ask a person
slides.notes: Ask what happens if every request is deferred. Coverage becomes zero, selective accuracy is unavailable, and full classifier quality remains unchanged. The model probabilities are not calibrated guarantees.

slides.title: Write the rule that sends a request to review
slides.notes: The function changes the displayed policy and the policy frozen for final evaluation. Its local check is free. Let people observe the coverage tradeoff rather than supply a preferred threshold.

slides.title: Read the disagreement before declaring failure
slides.notes: These four examples are actual outputs from the training-derived review pool. The published annotation is a reference, not proof that every message is unambiguous. The first two were selected as disagreements with the dataset annotation; the last two agree with it. They are not human review records. Let learners explain disagreement in their own words.

slides.title: Save labels someone can trace back to a decision
slides.notes: Show the provenance fields in the dataset artifact. Accepted human labels alone can extend training. Teacher suggestions and published-reference replay remain distinct. Encourage a discussion when participants disagree with the benchmark annotation.

slides.title: Break until 1:30
slides.notes: The break is ten minutes from elapsed 1:20 to 1:30. Ask people to leave the current page open. Restoring a saved checkpoint does not train or send model requests.

slides.title: A prompted model returns a typed decision
slides.notes: Run only eight preselected development requests. This sample teaches model behavior and trace inspection; it is too small to rank against classifiers evaluated on 3,080 final cases. The provider is fixed and charged to the participant allowance.

slides.title: Inspect eight actual model routes
slides.notes: Every request is durable and bounded. Each case gets a separate stage, so completed siblings can be reused after a failure. No test examples or accepted review labels enter the routing prompt.

slides.title: An automated failure tag needs its own evaluation
slides.notes: The notebook uses a model-based judge exercise. It is not silently creating native Agent Lens tags or pretending to generate Insights. Native tag alignment is an optional access-qualified extension. Prepared Insights require an independently verified cohort, not waiting live for new clusters.

slides.title: Implement the judge response check
slides.notes: The human accepted intent stays out of the judge prompt. The judge receives the request and proposed route. Check one reason, even if the JSON passes. Missing judgments stay missing; do not score them as correct or incorrect.

slides.title: The judge disagreed with the dataset label
slides.notes: The screenshot is an authenticated native capture. Its JSON pane clips the end of the reason; the caption quotes the full saved response. Both the request and failed:false are visible. Twelve development-only requests completed, their stored spans were verified, and observed inference cost was $0.00113494. Eight routing requests were an instrumentation sample, not a quality benchmark. Human review is still necessary.

slides.title: Use reviewed data to run a new experiment
slides.notes: The request review changes training data. It does not alter the encoder or hide difficult test examples. A review can be wrong, redundant, or too small to matter. Live improvement is measured, not scripted.

slides.title: Train with your accepted labels
slides.notes: This is the honest live experiment after the qualified representation improvement. Do not replace its result with the recorded gain. If labels disagree with the published annotation, inspect the text and the choice before attributing a score change to better data.

slides.title: Freeze what the final comparison will use
slides.notes: The notebook records the selected training stage and model checksum. A policy is part of the release decision and must be fixed before seeing the final requests. After final evaluation, another choice is a separately labeled teaching retest.

slides.title: Evaluate all matching test requests
slides.notes: All final predictions are retained. The selected model may equal the existing embedding model; that is a valid keep decision, not an invented third improvement. Keep classifier quality separate from deferral policy.

slides.title: Compare the same requests in Forge
slides.notes: Final evaluation publishes saved classifier predictions before the Report chapter. Click Compare in EvalTables. This is the native Weave-backed Evaluation Tables Preview in the W&B workspace. Aggregate macro-F1 remains computed from the whole prediction set; it is not the mean of row F1 scores.

slides.title: Read one routing decision
slides.notes: Use the saved case ID to match outputs. The automated judge comparison is separate and uses participant-reviewed development cases. Its target is agreement with those reviews, not classification accuracy on the official test set. The separate CES v2 service can remain unavailable while this Preview works.

slides.title: Write the decision you would make
slides.notes: Allow final ten minutes for pairs to explain one result. Publishing retries reuse saved executions. The report conclusion should be participant-authored. An improvement is welcome, but understanding a tie or regression completes the learning outcome.

slides.title: Reproduce the selected version before releasing it
slides.notes: The core ends with saved reproducible files and evaluation. Registry release and rollback is an advanced module with its own permissions. Specialist SFT changes model weights and needs a separate forecast and explicit launch; it is not required for this workshop.

slides.title: What to take back to your team
slides.notes: Close with a concrete transfer task. Ask each participant to name one queue, one failure, one measurable outcome, and one person who can review labels in their own workflow. No claims beyond the recorded Banking77 experiment.

slides.title: Worked answer: classifier head
slides.name: classifier-answer
slides.notes: Offer the answer only after an attempt or a hint request. Learners must still run the free check and both actual training calls.

slides.title: Worked answer: review policy
slides.name: policy-answer
slides.notes: The function should return a boolean. Exactly the threshold is routed in this specified policy. It is not a proof that the predicted probability is calibrated.

slides.title: Worked answer: judge validator
slides.name: validator-answer
slides.notes: The notebook worked answer also checks that value is a dictionary before reading its keys. Do not mistake passing this schema check for agreement with a human.

slides.title: Sources and recorded evidence
slides.notes: All measured claims come from the saved qualification. The native comparison captures show the verified routing publication and link to that saved record. Until external-account and human rehearsals pass, label this a technical preview.
